items.title: Topic Fourteen Opens: All Conditioned Things Arise and Cease — Their Quieting Is Bliss

items.zh: 諸行無常，有生滅法。由生滅故，彼寂為樂。
items.en: All conditioned things are impermanent — they are subject to arising and ceasing. Precisely because they arise and cease, their quieting is bliss.

items.zh: 今此頌中，蘊及取蘊皆名諸行。此中義者，意在取蘊。是五取蘊略有三種，謂去、來、今。諸行無常者，謂彼諸行本無而生，生已尋滅。若過去生，過去所得諸自體中所有諸蘊，皆過去故，已謝滅故，生已沒故，體是無常。若未來生，未來所得諸自體中所有諸蘊，皆未生故，非已起故，未滅沒故，可生起故，是有生法。若現在生，現在所得諸自體中所有暫住支持存活有情諸蘊，皆死法故，可為殞滅之所滅故，是有滅法。若彼諸蘊，在於未來所得自體，是有生法；於中都無所得自體是常、是恒，乃至即當如是正住。唯除纔生，生已尋滅。若諸有情於現法中，永盡未來諸蘊因者，一切未來自體諸蘊皆不生故，說名彼寂。又復此寂，由二因緣說之為樂。一者、一切苦因滅故，一切麁重永止息故，於現法中安樂住故，說之為樂。二者、當來生老病等所有眾苦永解脫故，說之為樂。復次，今當略辨上所說義。謂薄伽梵此中略說，正見依處及正見果。復有差別。謂略顯示遍知依處及彼斷滅。又略顯示所遍知法及與遍知。又略顯示三世諸行所有雜染，及彼寂故所有清淨。又略顯示諸緣起法及緣起滅。又略顯示苦諦、滅諦。又略顯示空與無願二解脫門所依處所，及顯無相一解脫門所依處所。又略顯示聖諦現觀相違二法斷所依處。言二法者，一、隨順戲論，二、怖無戲論。又略顯示不共外道二對治法。何等為二？一者、所知無顛倒性，二者、所證無顛倒性。
items.en: In this verse, the aggregates and the aggregates of grasping are both called formations. What is meant here is the aggregates of grasping. These five aggregates of grasping are, in brief, of three kinds: past, future, and present. 'Formations are impermanent' means that formations, having not existed, arise, and having arisen, soon cease. Those born in the past, the aggregates in the existences obtained in the past, are impermanent in nature because they are all past, have ceased, and having arisen have passed away. Those to be born in the future, the aggregates in the existences to be obtained in the future, are subject to arising because they have not yet arisen, have not yet appeared, have not yet ceased, and can arise. Those born in the present, the aggregates that for a while sustain and keep a being alive in the existence obtained in the present, are subject to ceasing because they are all subject to death and can be destroyed by perishing. Those aggregates in existences to be obtained in the future are subject to arising; among them there is no existence obtained that is permanent, constant, and so on up to remaining just as it is, except that as soon as they arise, having arisen they soon cease. If beings, in this present life, have exhausted for ever the causes of future aggregates, then, because all future existences and aggregates will not arise, they are said to be quieted. Further, this quieting is called bliss for two reasons. First, because all causes of suffering have ceased, all coarse burden has been stilled for ever, and one abides in happiness in this present life, it is called bliss. Second, because one is liberated for ever from all the sufferings of future birth, ageing, sickness, and the rest, it is called bliss. Further, the meaning of what was said above will now be briefly set out. Here the Blessed One briefly teaches the basis of right view and the fruit of right view. There is a further distinction: it briefly shows the basis of full knowledge and its abandonment. It briefly shows the dharmas to be fully known and the full knowledge of them. It briefly shows the defilement of formations in the three times and the purity that comes from their quieting. It briefly shows the dharmas of dependent arising and the cessation of dependent arising. It briefly shows the truth of suffering and the truth of cessation. It briefly shows the basis of the two gateways to liberation, emptiness and wishlessness, and the basis of the one gateway to liberation, signlessness. It briefly shows the basis for cutting off two dharmas that are contrary to direct realisation of the noble truths; the two dharmas are, first, following elaboration, and second, fearing the absence of elaboration. It also briefly shows two antidotes not shared with non-Buddhists. What are the two? First, freedom from distortion in what is to be known; second, freedom from distortion in what is to be realised.

items.title: Topic Fourteen, Sub-Part 2: Heedfulness Is the Path to Deathlessness

items.zh: 無逸不死跡；放逸為死跡。無逸者不死；縱逸者常死。
items.en: Heedfulness is the track to deathlessness; heedlessness is the track to death. The heedful do not die; the heedless die forever.

items.zh: 今此頌中，云何無放逸是不死迹耶？謂如有一，依四所依立四種護。謂命護、身護、心雜染護、正方便護。是名不放逸。此不放逸為依、為持，涅槃資糧未圓滿者，令速圓滿；已圓滿者，令於現法得般涅槃。云何放逸為死迹耶？謂如有一居家白衣，於諸欲境耽著受用，造不善業。或有出家，現四無護。謂命無護乃至正方便無護。如是放逸通於二品。謂在家品及出家品。即此放逸為依、為持，樂生本行，造生本業。因此故生，生已壽終，生已夭沒。云何無縱逸者不死，縱逸者常死耶？謂死有五種。一者、調善死，二者、不調善死，三者、過去死，四者、現在死，五者、未來死。若善修習此無縱逸補特伽羅，於現在世由調善死而正死時，由過去死已死，於過去世，亦由不調善死；於現在世，不由不調善死而死，於未來世，不由調善死，不由不調善死而死。故名不死。若有縱逸補特伽羅，於現在世由不調善死而正死時，於過去世，亦由不調善死已死；於現在世，即由不調善死而死；於未來世，亦由不調善死當死。故名常死。復次，今當略辨上所說義。謂薄伽梵此中略示，無縱逸者，道諦、滅諦；有縱逸者，集諦、苦諦。又略顯示處非處性、自業作性。前半顯示處非處性，後半顯示自業作性。又前半顯示師於弟子作所應作，後半顯示諸弟子等自所作義。
items.en: In this verse, how is heedfulness the track to deathlessness? Someone, relying on four supports, establishes four kinds of protection: protection of life, protection of the body, protection from defilement of mind, and protection of right means. This is called heedfulness. With this heedfulness as support and as holding, those whose provisions for nirvana are not yet complete quickly complete them, and those whose provisions are complete attain parinirvāṇa in this present life. How is heedlessness the track to death? Someone, a householder in white, indulges in and enjoys objects of sense desire and does unwholesome deeds. Or someone who has gone forth shows the four lacks of protection: no protection of life, and so on up to no protection of right means. Thus heedlessness covers two classes: the householder class and the class of those gone forth. With this heedlessness as support and as holding, they delight in the practices that are the root of birth and do the deeds that are the root of birth. Because of this they are born, and having been born their lives come to an end, or having been born they die young. How is it that the heedful do not die and the heedless always die? Death is of five kinds: first, tamed death; second, untamed death; third, past death; fourth, present death; fifth, future death. When a person who has cultivated heedfulness well dies a tamed death in the present life, then, as for past death, in past lives they died untamed deaths; in the present life they do not die an untamed death; and in future lives they will die neither a tamed nor an untamed death. So they are said not to die. When a heedless person dies an untamed death in the present life, then in past lives too they died untamed deaths; in the present life they die an untamed death; and in future lives too they will die untamed deaths. So they are said always to die. Further, the meaning of what was said above will now be briefly set out. Here the Blessed One briefly shows that for the heedful there are the truth of the path and the truth of cessation; for the heedless, the truth of origination and the truth of suffering. It also briefly shows what is possible and impossible, and the fact that one's own karma is one's own doing: the first half shows what is possible and impossible, the second half shows that one's own karma is one's own doing. Further, the first half shows the teacher doing for his disciples what should be done, and the second half shows what the disciples themselves must do.

blocks.text: Two of the most famous verses in Buddhism. Ru-Yi translates the verses; **the explanations are missing from Ru-Yi's translation** (0378c22–0379a22, 0379a25–b23). The English column gives our own translation, and the commentary summarises them.

"All conditioned things are impermanent; they are subject to arising and ceasing. Because they arise and cease, their quieting is bliss." Master Cháng Bǎi notes that these lines are placed first among such verses.

items: **What "conditioned things" means here:** the five aggregates of clinging, in the past, future, and present.

**Impermanent:** they arise from nothing, and having arisen soon cease. Past aggregates have ceased; future ones, not yet arisen, are "subject to arising"; present ones, which briefly sustain a being, are "subject to ceasing". In none of them is there any self that is permanent or lasting.

**Quieting:** when the causes of future aggregates are exhausted in this life, future aggregates no longer arise: that is "quieting". It is **bliss** for two reasons: all causes of suffering and all heaviness cease, so one dwells at ease now; and one is free of future birth, ageing, and sickness.

**In brief,** the verse shows the basis of right view and its result; what is to be fully known and its full knowledge; defilement and purification; dependent origination and its cessation; the truths of suffering and cessation; the bases of the three doors of liberation.

blocks.text: Venerable Miào Jìng: the first three lines are dependent origination, conventional truth; "their quieting is bliss" is ultimate truth. Master Cháng Bǎi: we cannot bear loss of what is "mine"; the arhat has no "mine", so the quieting is bliss.

"Heedfulness is the track to deathlessness; heedlessness is the track to death. The heedful do not die; the heedless die forever." Master Cháng Bǎi: a track is the trace left on a muddy road: a path and a cause.

items: **Heedfulness** means guarding four things: one's life, one's body, the mind against defilement, and right effort. It completes the provisions for nirvāṇa.
**Heedlessness** is the householder indulging in pleasures and doing harm, or a renunciant who guards none of the four; it leads to repeated birth and death.

**Five deaths:** tamed death, untamed death, and past, present, future deaths. The heedful person dies a tamed death now, and in the future no death at all: "deathless". The heedless died untamed in the past, die untamed now, and will die untamed again: "they die forever".

blocks.text: Master Cháng Bǎi: thinking "I'll study the Dharma when I retire" is itself heedlessness.

quiz.q: What are the four lines of the first verse of the discourse topic?
options: do no evil, practice good, purify the mind
all conditioned things are impermanent, subject to arising and ceasing; because they arise and cease, their quieting is bliss
all conditioned things are like a dream
what arises from conditions I call emptiness
quiz.why: The verse: all conditioned things are impermanent — they are subject to arising and ceasing; because they arise and cease, their quieting is bliss. Master Cháng Bǎi: these four lines are placed first among the verses of discourse because they are the essence of the Dharma.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi relate momentary arising-and-ceasing to the arising-and-ceasing of a lifetime?
options: the aggregates arise and cease moment by moment, and because of that there is the arising and ceasing of a lifetime
momentary change belongs only to noble ones
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: in fact the five aggregates of clinging arise and cease moment by moment; it is because of momentary arising and ceasing that there is the arising and ceasing of a lifetime — hence "having arisen, they soon cease."

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng map the four lines onto the two truths?
options: the first three lines are dependent origination, conventional truth; "their quieting is bliss" is ultimate truth
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "all conditioned things are impermanent, subject to arising and ceasing, because they arise and cease" is dependent origination, conventional truth; "their quieting is bliss" — the quieting is ultimate truth. He adds that impermanence implies no-self and points to the emptiness gate of liberation.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi describe an ordinary being's attitude towards impermanence?
options: ordinary beings do not fear it
what concerns you, you can't bear; what doesn't, you don't care about
they fear only their own death
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi, citing the Āgama simile of the bowl: what concerns you, you cannot bear; what does not concern you, you do not care about. That is love of what is "mine"; the arhat has no "mine," and so the quieting is bliss.

quiz.q: How do the two masters explain 跡 in "heedfulness is the track to deathlessness"?
options: the trace left by walking on mud — really a road, and also a cause
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: a track is the trace left walking across mud — it is a road and also a cause; heedfulness is a cause for attaining nirvāṇa. Venerable Miào Jìng: the track is the trace that appears from walking on a road — really it means the road itself.

quiz.q: According to the verse, what becomes of the heedless?
options: heedlessness is the track to death; the heedless die forever
quiz.why: "Heedlessness is the track to death... the heedless die forever." Master Cháng Bǎi: an ordinary being dies untamed in past, present, and future — hence "forever"; an arhat has no future death — hence "deathless."

quiz.q: What kind of thinking does Master Cháng Bǎi call heedless?
options: waiting until retirement or old age to study the Dharma, as if it were for the elderly
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: many people think, "I won't study the Dharma for now — I'll wait until I retire, until I'm older; Buddhism is for old people." Thinking this way is heedlessness. He illustrates with the lazy farmer who missed six chances to hear the Buddha.
